$comment: Transmit application catalog. Each entry says how to recognise an application on each platform, how to reinstall it, which directories hold its state, and which files inside that state contain paths that must be rewritten for the new machine. Drop additional files into the user catalog directory to extend or correct this.

apps.name: Alacritty
apps.note: The font named in the configuration may not exist on the new system; the report will say so if it had to fall back.

apps.name: AnyDesk
apps.note: The AnyDesk identity is tied to the machine, so this one gets a new address.

apps.name: Bash
apps.note: Shell configuration often names tools and paths from the old machine; the report lists what could not be resolved here.

apps.name: calibre
apps.note: The library folder itself is ordinary files; make sure it is in the selection if it lives outside your documents.

apps.name: DBeaver
apps.note: Connection definitions travel; the saved passwords for them are protected by the old machine and need re-entering.

apps.name: Docker configuration
apps.note: Only the client configuration travels. Images and containers are tied to the machine that built them and are rebuilt or pulled again.

apps.name: Element
apps.note: Element stores its encryption keys per device. Verify this as a new session from another device rather than expecting the old keys to work.

apps.name: Emacs
apps.note: Byte-compiled and natively compiled files are left behind because they are built for the old machine; Emacs regenerates them.

apps.name: Figma
apps.note: Your files live in your Figma account, so they are there as soon as you sign in.

apps.name: File manager bookmarks
apps.note: Bookmarked folders are repointed at where those folders landed on this machine.

apps.name: Firefox
apps.note: Firefox keeps saved passwords in key4.db next to logins.json, both inside the profile, so they travel with it and keep working on the new system.

apps.name: Git
apps.note: Paths inside the configuration are repointed. A credential helper named there is specific to the old system and is reported for you to set again.

apps.name: GnuPG
apps.note: Your keyring travels. Private keys are restored with owner-only permissions, which GnuPG insists on before it will use them.

apps.name: Google Chrome
apps.note: Chrome seals its saved passwords with a key held by the operating system, so those need the credentials option; bookmarks, history, extensions and settings move as they are.

apps.name: JetBrains IDEs
apps.note: Keymaps, colour schemes and inspection profiles carry across. Project indexes are rebuilt on first open and are deliberately not copied.

apps.name: KDE Connect
apps.note: Paired devices are identified by a per-machine key, so pair this machine again.

apps.name: KeePassXC
apps.note: The password database is a file of your own; make sure it is in the selection, and the recent-files list is repointed at where it landed.

apps.name: LibreOffice
apps.note: Templates, autocorrect entries, macros and your custom dictionary all travel.

apps.name: npm settings
apps.note: An access token in .npmrc is carried across as written; rotate it if the new machine is not equally trusted.

apps.name: OBS Studio
apps.note: Scenes and settings carry across. Sources that name a capture device or a window will need repointing on the new machine.

apps.name: Obsidian
apps.note: The list of vaults is repointed at where those folders landed here. The notes themselves come across as ordinary files.

apps.name: PuTTY
apps.note: PuTTY keeps its sessions in the Windows registry. Export them with "regedit /e" before the move; Transmit cannot read them from the filesystem.

apps.name: Python packaging settings
apps.note: Virtual environments contain compiled binaries and are excluded; recreate them from your requirements file.

apps.name: rclone
apps.note: Remote definitions include access tokens. They are carried as written, so treat the archive accordingly.

apps.name: Rust toolchain settings
apps.note: The configuration travels; run rustup again on the new machine to fetch the toolchains, which are compiled for the old one.

apps.name: Signal Desktop
apps.note: Signal encrypts its message database with a key held by the operating system's keychain, so the history usually cannot follow. Re-link the desktop app from your phone instead.

apps.name: Slack
apps.note: You will be asked to sign in again: the session token is tied to the machine it was issued on.

apps.name: Spotify
apps.note: Playlists live in your account, not on the machine, so they are there when you sign in. Downloaded offline tracks stay behind.

apps.name: SSH keys and configuration
apps.note: Private keys are only readable by you, and Transmit restores that. On Windows the permission model differs, so check the keys are accepted before relying on them.

apps.name: Steam
apps.note: Local settings and cloud-save staging travel. The games themselves are platform-specific and must be downloaded again from your library.

apps.name: Syncthing
apps.note: The device identity travels, so your other devices still recognise this one. Folder paths are repointed at where those folders landed here.

apps.name: Telegram Desktop
apps.note: The signed-in session travels with the data directory, so you stay logged in.

apps.name: Thunderbird
apps.note: Local mail folders are carried across. The account passwords live in the profile for Thunderbird, so they survive the move.

apps.name: Tor Browser
apps.note: Tor Browser is deliberately built to leave no portable identity. Install it fresh rather than carrying its profile over.

apps.name: VirtualBox
apps.note: Only the preferences travel. Virtual machine disks are very large and are excluded by default; copy them yourself if you need them.

apps.name: Visual Studio Code
apps.note: Extensions are carried across as files. Any that ship compiled native components will need reinstalling on a different operating system.

apps.name: Zsh and Oh My Zsh
apps.note: Shell configuration often names paths and tools that exist only on the old machine; those lines are reported so you can adjust them.
